title: LeLy Study (Living with Lynch Study): The Situation of People with Lynch Syndrome in Germany
summary:
Lynch syndrome is the most common hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome and is associated with a substantially increased lifetime risk of developing various cancers, particularly colorectal cancer, endometrial cancer, and ovarian cancer. Despite its clinical relevance, an estimated only approximately 10 percent of affected individuals in Germany have received a diagnosis. To date, no systematic data are available on the healthcare situation, level of disease-related knowledge, or the impact on life planning and quality of life among people with Lynch syndrome in Germany.

The LeLy Study investigates how people with a confirmed diagnosis of Lynch syndrome in Germany are being cared for medically, how well informed they are about their condition, and how Lynch syndrome affects their lives. The study uses an anonymous cross-sectional online design. Adults with a confirmed Lynch syndrome diagnosis are asked to complete a self-developed online questionnaire on a single occasion. The questionnaire covers medical care, use of recommended cancer surveillance examinations, information-seeking behaviour, impact on life planning and quality of life, and attitudes towards digital medicine. Data will be analysed using descriptive and exploratory methods.

Observational study
1 arm (no comparison group)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Minimum age 18 years
Confirmed diagnosis of Lynch syndrome
Informed consent to participate in the study
Sufficient command of the German language to independently read and complete the study information, informed consent form, and online questionnaire
Exclusion criteria:
Minors (under 18 years of age)
Absence of informed consent
Insufficient command of the German language to independently participate in the German-language online survey
